newsitem.title: USA: Simpson case filled with tales of murder, conspiracy.
newsitem.headline: Simpson case filled with tales of murder, conspiracy.

text.p: The following is a chronology of events in the O.J. Simpson double-murder case:
June 13 - The bodies of Nicole Brown Simpson and her friend Ronald Goldman are found outside her townhouse. O.J. Simpson returns from Chicago and is questioned by police.
June 16 - Victims are buried in separate ceremonies.
June 17 - Simpson is arrested after nationally televised slow-speed chase along Los Angeles freeways.
June 20 - Simpson pleads not guilty.
June 30 - Simpson's preliminary hearing begins.
July 8 - Judge orders Simpson to stand trial.
July 20 - Simpson offers $500,000 reward for information leading to the "real killer or killers." Goldman's mother, Sharon Rufo, files wrongful death lawsuit against Simpson.
July 22 - Simpson pleads "absolutely, 100 percent not guilty" at his arraignment. Case assigned to Judge Lance Ito.
Sept. 9 - Los Angeles district attorney's office says it will not seek death penalty against Simpson.
Sept. 26 - Jury selection begins.
Jan. 11 - Jury sequestered.
Jan. 24 - Opening statements begin.
Feb. 12 - Jury tours crime scene and Simpson's mansion.
Mar. 9 - Detective Mark Fuhrman takes the witness stand to testify about finding bloody glove at Simpson's estate.
May 5 - Goldman's father, Fred Goldman, files wrongful death lawsuit against Simpson.
May 12 - Nicole's father, Louis Brown, files a wrongful death lawsuit against Simpson for Nicole's estate.
June 15 - Simpson tries on bloody gloves in court and pronounces them "too small."
Aug. 29 - Portions of taped interviews with Fuhrman played in court in which he is heard uttering racial slurs.
Sept. 6 - Taking the witness stand with jury absent, Fuhrman asserts constitutional right against self-incrimination and refuses to answer questions.
Sept. 22 - Simpson proclaims his innocence in a surprise courtroom statement; both sides rest.
Sept. 25 - Closing arguments begin.
Sept. 29 - Case is handed over to jury.
Oct. 2 - Jury reaches verdict after less than three hours of deliberations. Ito says verdict to be read next day.
Oct. 3 - Simpson is acquitted and set free.
Jan. 22 - Lawyers for plaintiffs begin taking Simpson's sworn deposition.
Jan. 25 - In first full post-trial TV interview, Simpson tells a Black Entertainment Television reporter that he is innocent.
July 17 - Judge Alan Haber, who presided over pre-trial issues, is removed from case at request of Simpson's lawyers.
July 23 - Judge Hiroshi Fujisaki assigned to civil case.
Aug. 13 -- Fujisaki imposes sweeping gag order.
Aug. 23 - Fujisaki bans all cameras from courtroom.
Sept. 17 - Civil trial begins.
Sept. 18 - Jury selection starts.
Oct. 23 - Openings statements begin with Goldman family attorney calling Simpson a "vengeful killer."
Nov. 22 - Simpson takes witness stand.
Nov. 26 - Simpson ends three days of testimony without a single question from his own attorneys.
Jan. 10 - Simpson returns to witness stand, this time under gentler questioning by his defence team.
Jan. 21 - Closing arguments begin.
Jan. 28 - Case goes to jury.
Jan. 31 - Judge dismisses only black member of the jury and orders deliberations to start over as investigators looked into allegations of jury tampering.
Feb. 4 - Sixteen months after Simpson cleared of murder charges, mostly white jury blames Simpson for the killings and orders him to pay $8.5 million in compensatory damages.
